hero_body: AtoA prepares personal, family and small‑business tax returns in English, Arabic, Swahili and French. Sit down with someone who speaks your language, understand every line before you sign, and leave knowing what comes next.
card1: W‑2s, 1099s and IDs, all on the checklist
card2: Every form checked against last year
card3: Child tax credit and EITC reviewed
card5: The IRS and Iowa accepted the e‑file
card_footer: Refund sent to the family's own account
s_title: Taxes for people first. Businesses too.
s_body: Most of our clients are individuals and families. Whatever your situation, we've likely seen it before, and we'll explain it in the language you're most comfortable with.
svc1_b: Federal and state returns for workers, families, students and retirees, with every credit you qualify for: child tax credit, earned income credit, education credits.
svc2_t: Live in Illinois, work in Iowa (or the reverse)
svc2_b: The two states have an agreement for wages. We make sure only one state taxes your paycheck, and get back tax that the wrong state withheld.
svc3_b: Rideshare and delivery drivers, truckers, home daycare, cleaning, hair and beauty. We count your mileage and expenses so you pay tax on your profit, not on everything the app reports.
svc4_b: Help with Form W‑7 for a spouse or children who can't get a Social Security number, filed together with your return. We'll explain how to send your ID documents to the IRS (originals or certified copies) or where to have them checked in person.
svc5_b: Didn't file last year, or found a mistake? We prepare late and amended returns and help you get back on track.
svc6_b: Bring the letter. We'll read it with you, explain what it means in your language, and help you answer before the deadline.
svc7_b: For owners of LLCs, partnerships and S corporations: the business return, quarterly estimates and the owner's personal return, all in one place.
l_title: Four languages, and nothing lost in translation.
l_body: Taxes are hard enough in your first language. AtoA is the Quad Cities tax office where Arabic, Swahili, French and English speakers talk directly with the person preparing their return. No interpreter needed.
l_note: Family members are welcome to come with you. We explain everything to the person signing, in the language they choose.
p_title: From A to A: from your first document to an accepted return.
p_body: Five steps, and you'll always know which one you're on.
p1: Bring your documents. The checklist below shows exactly what you need.
p2: We check every W‑2, 1099 and receipt, and compare them with last year's return.
p3: We apply every deduction and credit you qualify for, and explain the ones you don't.
p4: We go through your return line by line, in your language. Nothing is filed until you sign.
p5: We e‑file your federal and state returns and send you proof once they're accepted.
b_body: Tick off what you have. Not sure about a paper? Bring it anyway. It's easier to set one aside than to wait for one that's missing.
b1_items: Photo ID for you and your spouse
Social Security cards or ITIN letters for everyone on the return
Bank account and routing number for your refund
b2_items: 1099‑NEC or 1099‑K from apps like Uber, Lyft or DoorDash
SSA‑1099 or 1099‑R for Social Security or a pension
b3_items: Childcare provider's name, address, tax ID and the amount you paid
1095‑A if you have insurance from HealthCare.gov
1098 for mortgage interest, and your property tax
b4_items: Total income from your work or apps
Receipts for supplies, phone and equipment
Any estimated tax payments you made
b_note: Received a letter from the IRS or the state? Bring that too.
t_body: The IRS warns about “ghost preparers”: people who charge to do your taxes, don't sign the return, and disappear when there's a problem. Newcomers and families are common targets. Here's how we work, and the warning signs to watch for anywhere.
t_link: IRS guide: how to choose a tax preparer
t_promises: We sign every return we prepare, with our IRS preparer number (PTIN).
Your refund goes only to your own bank account.
Our fee is never a percentage of your refund.
You get a copy of everything you sign.
We tell you the fee before we start.
t_warnings: The preparer won't sign the return.
You're asked to sign a blank or unfinished form.
A big refund is promised before anyone sees your papers.
Your refund goes to someone else's account.
d_body: Missing a date can mean penalties. If you're running late, call us early: an extension can often help.
d2: Employers must send W‑2s and 1099s by today
d3: Federal and Illinois returns due, or ask for an extension
faq_items: Do I need to speak English?
No. You can do the whole appointment in Arabic, Swahili, French or English. The forms are in English, as the IRS requires, but we explain every line in your language.
I live in Illinois and work in Iowa. Do I file two state returns?

Usually just one. Iowa and Illinois have an agreement that taxes wages only in the state where you live. If the wrong state took tax from your paycheck, we file to get it back and show you how to fix it with your employer.
My spouse or child doesn't have a Social Security number.

They may be able to get an ITIN, a tax number from the IRS. We can help with the application (Form W‑7) and send it with your return. We'll explain how to send your ID documents to the IRS (originals or certified copies) or where to have them checked in person.
I drive for Uber, Lyft or DoorDash. What do I need?
The yearly summary from each app and a record of the miles you drove for work. Mileage often lowers your tax a lot, so even a rough record helps.
It depends on your return, so we tell you the fee before we start. It's never a percentage of your refund.
When will I get my refund?

The IRS says most e‑filed returns with direct deposit are refunded within 21 days. By law, refunds that include the earned income credit or the additional child tax credit can't be sent before mid‑February.
Can I bring a family member?
Of course. Many clients come with a spouse, a parent or a grown child.
